title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, billing qualifications and documented controls are supported. Both API requests match their Microsoft references, including the allocation request body and the deprecated consumption endpoint; targeted searches did not establish the node-specific controls reported as undocumented.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: An agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent that can reason over its inputs.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The agent can call attached tools to take actions.
claims.quote: Tools give the agent the ability to do actions such as send a message, query a record, run a search, or call an API.

claims.claim: The agent can read attached knowledge sources to ground its response.
claims.quote: When you ask the agent a question, it can ground its answer in the sources you attach instead of relying only on what the model already knows.

claims.claim: The agent's result becomes dynamic content available to subsequent workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, go to Workflows and open an existing workflow, or create a new one. Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the Build tab. Select the Agent icon on the Add panel.

claims.claim: An existing agent selects a published agent from a list.
claims.quote: An existing agent: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow builds an inline agent configured inside the node.
claims.quote: New agent for this workflow: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow.

claims.claim: The inline agent's instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape travel with the workflow.
claims.quote: The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent cannot be reused outside its workflow.
claims.quote: Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow? No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.claim: MCP servers are a supported kind of attached tool.
claims.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: Prebuilt servers that expose a curated set of capabilities.

claims.claim: Any Power Platform connector action can be attached as a tool.

claims.claim: Public websites are supported knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Public websites: Index one or more public URLs so the agent can cite content from those sites.

claims.claim: SharePoint sites and their content can ground an inline agent.
claims.quote: SharePoint: Connect to a SharePoint site, library, or specific document so the agent can answer from internal content.

claims.quote: Turn on Work IQ to let the agent use the running user's recent work activity, including mail, Teams, calendar, OneDrive, and SharePoint context, to ground its responses.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and allocation paragraph
claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the environment allocation with the supplied JSON body.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: The complete allocation body uses scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements containing MCSMessages, allocation.quantity and enforcementRules with TenantPool disabled.
The TenantPool rule with enabled false turns off the environment's draw from unallocated tenant capacity.
claims.quote:
enforcementRules = @(
                # Disable TenantPool so the environment is capped at its allocation.
                # Set enabled = $true to let the environment draw from tenant capacity.
                @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }

claims.claim: The allocation request requires authenticated authorisation.
claims.quote:
$auth = Get-MsalToken -ClientId $clientId -TenantId $tenantId -Scope "https://api.powerplatform.com/.default" -Interactive
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" }

claims.claim: The allocation request uses Content-Type: application/json.
claims.quote: -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: An environment-group rule governing tenant draw makes the environment setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic allocation requests cannot override an environment group's tenant-draw rule.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Eligible Copilot Studio environments default to drawing from tenant capacity when no allocation configuration exists.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, Draw from the available capacity in my tenant is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.
